Programme: [#2056](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/2056). +- **Settled siblings this record builds on:** [#5853](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5853) + (`doc/2026-11-08_decision_id5853_custom_gui_rendering_overrides.md`), + [#5852](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5852) + (`doc/2026-11-08_decision_id5852_native_rendering_os_standard_controls.md`), + [#5854](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5854) + (`doc/2026-11-08_decision_id5854_per_target_composition.md`), and the + output-safety contract of [#5785](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5785) + (`doc/2026-11-08_design_id5785.md`). Every one of those records assumes + a vocabulary of "semantic elements"; this record is that vocabulary. +- **Still-open siblings whose seams this record names but does not + decide:** [#5850](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5850) + (style assertion vocabulary — the `assert` slot, §7), + [#5851](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5851) + (web mapping — element → DOM/classes, §5), and + [#5855](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5855) + (pipeline and conformance suite, §10). +- **Evidence baseline:** `origin/main` at `30bd3a1398`, 2026-11-08 + (task 13590). Fresh reads: issue #5849 OPEN, no hard-stop labels; + parent #5679 OPEN; siblings #5850, #5851, #5855 OPEN, #5852, #5853, + #5854 CLOSED with their records on `main`; issue #5849 has no linked + PR and no decision record. `git grep -iE 'semantic (markup|element)| + element kind|programs-as-websites'` over `pkgs/id/src` and + `pkgs/id/crates` returns no registry, parser, or vocabulary type, so + this record is the first decision for this follow-on rather than a + description of existing code. Source issue #2146 (closed) supplies + the serving context the parent extends. + +## Decision summary + +| Question | Decision | +| --- | --- | +| Authoring syntax | **HTML-shaped source from a closed registry**: element names and attributes follow HTML vocabulary where an HTML equivalent exists, values are always quoted attributes, and content is text. One semantic dialect, no second syntax to learn (§2) | +| How raw HTML coexists | Raw HTML is admitted **only inside an explicit `` region** (and raw CSS in ``); a tag outside the registry is a **build-time error naming the nearest registry entries**, never an implicit raw pass-through (§3) | +| Element set | **Closed v1 registry of 32 elements** in four groups — document/structure, inline text, forms/actions, application chrome (§4) | +| Versioning | Source declares `version="1"` on `document`; adding, renaming, or removing an element is a version change, and v1 parsers reject unknown versions (§2.4) | +| Target coverage | Every registry element must be renderable on **web, custom-GUI, and native targets** in its standard rendering; no element is web-only. Elements that could not be given a defensible native/GUI meaning are **deferred**, not shipped as web-only (§5) | +| Accessibility | Role, accessible-name source, allowed states, and keyboard contract are **properties of the element kind**, not attributes an author may omit. Authoring checks them at build time (§6) | +| Styling seam | Style assertions attach through **one `assert` attribute slot per element**; the assertion grammar and vocabulary are #5850's, the cascade is #5854's. The vocabulary never names a colour, size, or variant (§7) | +| State and actions | A fixed set of **binding slots** (`bind`, `items`, `show`, `disabled-when`, `action`, `on-*`) whose values are names in the program's declared state/action table. No expressions, no code, no target-specific syntax in source (§8) | +| Data safety | Every value the vocabulary carries enters only a text, quoted-attribute, or sanitized-URL context per #5785 §1; **no script context exists in the vocabulary**, and guest-emitted output is never parsed as source (§3.3) | +| Deferred | Trees, charts, carousels, rich-text editing, canvas/drawing, maps, spreadsheets, command palettes, drag-and-drop, regex validation, and i18n interpolation are named out of v1 with reasons (§9) | + +## 1. What is already fixed (not re-decided here) + +1. **Parent #5679:** two layers — raw HTML/CSS always supported, never + gated; semantic markup describes *intent and structure*, not + presentation; accessibility role is intrinsic per element; one + content/semantic source per programme; authoring ergonomics mean + "writable by hand, diff-friendly, a strict subset in spirit of what + HTML authors already know (names/attributes mapped from HTML where + possible)"; data binding must connect to state and actions "without + embedding target-specific code". +2. **#5853:** presentation overrides bind by element instance or by + **element kind + variant/emphasis role + state set**, and must cover + the element kind's **full state set**. That record already treats + "element kind" and "state set" as registry concepts; this record + defines both. +3. **#5852:** native rendering maps each element kind to an OS-standard + control and each assertion dimension per platform; it assumes every + element has a native control, a state set, and an accessible name. +4. **#5854:** the cascade is platform defaults → theme tokens → + assertions → override map → raw CSS (web only); conditional blocks + are evaluated before the cascade; raw CSS is ignored with a warning + off the web target. +5. **#5785:** a data value enters markup only in a text, quoted-attribute, + or sanitized-URL context, never a script context; stored or forwarded + data is never evaluated downstream. +6. Nothing in §2–§9 changes any of the above. §11 says so explicitly and + names the questions that would. + +## 2. Authoring syntax (the decision) + +### 2.1 The source is HTML-shaped, not HTML + +The semantic source is a single text document whose elements are +written like HTML: + +```text + + + Account settings +
+ + + Name is required. + +
+ + +``` + +Rules that make this the decision rather than a preference: + +- **Closed registry.** Only element names in §4 parse; only the + attributes listed for that element parse. An unknown element or + attribute is a build error, not a warning and not a silent fallback + (§3.2). +- **Names come from HTML where HTML has the concept.** `page`, + `section`, `nav`, `heading`, `text`, `list`, `item`, `link`, `image`, + `card`, `table`, `row`, `cell`, `form`, `field`, `button`, `dialog` + are deliberately the HTML names for the HTML concepts, so an HTML + author's intuition transfers and a reader can guess an element's + meaning. Where no HTML element means the right thing (`master-detail`, + `preference`, `tabs`, `tab`), the name is the plainest English word + for the concept. +- **Quoted attributes only.** Attribute values are always double-quoted; + unquoted attribute syntax does not exist in the grammar. This is + #5785 §1's attribute-context rule made syntactic, so the escaper's + guarantee cannot be sidestepped by an author. +- **Text is content.** Element content is text (escaped at render per + #5785 §1) plus child elements from the registry. Inline emphasis is + carried by `strong` and `emphasis` children of `text`, never by + attribute-driven markup. +- **No presentation attributes.** There is no `class`, `style`, `width`, + `color`, or `align` attribute anywhere in the registry. Appearance is + assertions (§7) and per-target overrides (#5854). An HTML-shaped + author who reaches for `style` gets a build error that points at the + `assert` slot. +- **Comments** use ``, matching HTML, and are stripped at + build time. They may not contain elements. +- **Whitespace between elements is insignificant**; whitespace inside + `text` is collapsed to single spaces and leading/trailing whitespace + trimmed, so reflowing a paragraph produces a clean diff. + +### 2.2 Why not a Markdown-adjacent syntax or an s-expression DSL + +Markdown is excellent for prose and poor for the application chrome +this vocabulary must also express: a form with bound fields and +validation, tabs, a master-detail pane, a settings sheet. Encoding +those in Markdown means either fenced directives that are HTML-shaped +anyway, or attribute syntax that is less regular than attributes. An +s-expression form is regular and precise, but it is a second thing to +learn for an HTML-literate audience, it diffs worse for prose-heavy +text, and it makes the raw-HTML escape hatch read as a foreign island +rather than a sibling. §10 records both as rejected alternatives with +the costs accepted in exchange. + +### 2.3 Hand-authorability and diff-friendliness + +- One element per line is not required, but every element is + independently parseable and independently reflowable: wrapping a long + attribute list or a long paragraph never changes the tree. +- Elements have no required closing-tag ceremony beyond the closing tag + itself; self-closing form (``) is accepted wherever an + element has no children, and the formatter emits the self-closing + form for empty elements only. +- No construct depends on column position, indentation, or ordering. + Source order is meaningful only where the registry says so (sibling + order is reading order and focus order, §6). + +### 2.4 Versioning + +`document` requires `version`. v1 parsers accept `version="1"` and +reject any other value with a build error naming the supported +versions. Adding an element, renaming one, changing an element's state +set, or changing a binding slot's type is a version change; widening +what an existing element accepts (an optional attribute, an extra field +kind) is a compatible v1 change recorded in the registry changelog the +pipeline ships (#5855). + +## 3. Raw HTML and the boundary with emitted output + +### 3.1 The one raw region + +Raw HTML lives in exactly one place: + +```text +
…
 +.ascii-art { font-family: monospace } +``` + +- Content of `` is passed through verbatim to the web + target and degrades per #5854 §2.3 on GUI/native targets (author + fallback, or the target's webview embedding where #5851/#5852 allow + it). +- Content of `` is the raw-CSS layer of #5854 §2.1 — + highest precedence on web only, ignored with a build-time warning + elsewhere. +- `raw` regions are recognised syntactically, so the parser never has to + guess whether a tag was meant as HTML or as vocabulary. Authors who + want raw HTML write it inside the region; the region is greppable, so + a reviewer can see every escape hatch in one search. +- `raw` content is **authored source**, not data. It is never populated + from a bound value (§3.3). + +### 3.2 No implicit raw, no silent fallback + +A tag outside the registry is a build error that lists the three nearest +registry names with their one-line purposes. It is never treated as raw +HTML. The reason is determinism: a typo (``) silently becoming a +raw HTML tag would change an element from semantic (accessibility role, +native control) to inert markup, and the failure would show up as a +missing control on native targets rather than at build time.
